title: Legacy TLS & Crypto Protocol
description: Older TLS protocol and certificate weaknesses that affect transport trust.

attacks.name: POODLE
attacks.desc: POODLE exploits SSLv3 CBC padding behavior when a connection falls back to the obsolete protocol.
attacks.prevention: Disable SSLv3 and fallback to it; support current TLS versions with maintained cipher configurations.

attacks.name: BEAST
attacks.desc: BEAST targets predictable CBC chaining in TLS 1.0 under conditions that allow chosen plaintext.
attacks.prevention: Disable TLS 1.0 and legacy CBC suites where compatibility allows, and use modern AEAD cipher suites.

attacks.name: Heartbleed
attacks.desc: Heartbleed is an OpenSSL heartbeat bug that can disclose process memory from an affected server.
attacks.prevention: Patch affected OpenSSL builds, rotate exposed private keys where necessary, and disable vulnerable heartbeat support.

attacks.name: DROWN
attacks.desc: DROWN uses an SSLv2-capable service sharing an RSA key to weaken otherwise stronger TLS connections.
attacks.prevention: Disable SSLv2 on all services sharing a certificate key and replace weak or reused RSA keys.

attacks.name: ROBOT
attacks.desc: ROBOT relies on a Bleichenbacher-style RSA padding oracle in vulnerable TLS implementations.

attacks.name: Lucky13
attacks.desc: Lucky13 uses CBC record-processing timing differences to infer protected plaintext in affected implementations.

attacks.name: Sweet32
attacks.desc: Sweet32 exploits birthday collisions in 64-bit block ciphers during long encrypted sessions.

attacks.name: FREAK / Logjam
attacks.desc: FREAK and Logjam exploit support for weak export-grade key exchange or related downgrade paths.

attacks.name: CRIME
attacks.desc: CRIME can reveal secrets when TLS compression makes ciphertext length depend on attacker-controlled input.

attacks.name: RC4 bias
attacks.desc: Statistical biases in RC4 output can weaken confidentiality when a service still offers RC4 ciphers.

attacks.name: Cert misissuance
attacks.desc: Certificate transparency records can reveal certificates issued unexpectedly for a domain.

attacks.name: OCSP stapling absence
attacks.desc: Missing OCSP stapling shifts revocation checking to the client and may affect privacy or availability; it is not a standalone compromise.
